hints: Focus on counting carbons first, then work out hydrogens from the skeletal structures, remembering each carbon needs four bonds.
Notice that a ketone C=O carbon has no hydrogens, an alkene CH= has one hydrogen, and remember to add methyl and OH groups carefully.
Check each structure for a total of 6 carbons, 10 hydrogens and 1 oxygen, and see which one matches all three counts exactly.
walkthrough:
**Recall how to count from skeletal structures**

Each corner and end of a line is a carbon. Hydrogens are hidden, so give each carbon enough H to make 4 bonds in total.

Rule: $H \text{ on C} = 4 - (\text{bonds shown to C and other atoms})$

**Count option A**

This is 3-methylcyclopentanone. Ring has 5 C plus 1 C in methyl, so 6 C total.

Ring H: $C=O = 0H, 2 \times CH_2 \text{ next to } C=O = 4H, CH(CH_3) = 1H, CH_2 = 2H$ gives 7H, plus $CH_3 = 3H$. Total is $C_6H_{10}O$.

**Count the others and conclude**

Option B is $CH_3COC(CH_3)_3$ with $3H + 9H = 12H$, so $C_6H_{12}O$. Option C is cyclohex-2-en-1-one with two alkene $CH$ groups, so $C_6H_8O$. Option D is an unsaturated alcohol with $C_6H_{12}O$.

Only the methylcyclopentanone fits $C_6H_{10}O$ exactly.

options.A: Correct. 5 ring carbons + 1 methyl carbon = 6 C. Hydrogens are 2+1+2+2 on the ring = 7H plus 3H on methyl = 10H, with one ketone O. This gives C6H10O exactly.
options.B: Incorrect. This is 3,3-dimethylbutan-2-one, CH3COC(CH3)3. It has 6 C and 1 O but 3 + 9 = 12 H, so C6H12O. The trap is counting carbons only and forgetting the extra hydrogens on the tert-butyl group.
options.C: Incorrect. This is cyclohex-2-en-1-one. It has 6 C and 1 O but contains one C=C double bond which removes 2 H compared to the saturated ketone, giving C6H8O. The trap is missing the effect of the double bond on H count.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 2,3-dimethylbut-3-en-1-ol. It has 6 C and 1 O but only one double bond, so it is C6H12O. The trap is thinking one double bond plus one OH gives C6H10O, but an alcohol with one alkene still has 12 H.
